nodes.label: Iron laws (capability denials)
nodes.rationale: Framed as capability denials rather than advice so they cannot be traded away under pressure; only an explicit user message in the current conversation can lift one, because standing instructions and config files are exactly the channels a model would otherwise use to rationalize an exception.

nodes.label: Before acting: one-line task classification
nodes.rationale: Naming the task type (debug | implement | investigate | review | trivial) before the first edit selects which playbook applies, so the method is chosen before momentum makes the choice.

nodes.label: Completion gate (name, predict, run, read, show)
nodes.rationale: Predicting the outcome in writing before running turns a green run into a test of the model's model of the system; an unpredicted green run proves less than it feels, and a surprise is treated as a signal to investigate rather than to claim success.

nodes.label: Claim-to-evidence table
nodes.rationale: Pairs each claim type (bug fixed, tests pass, feature works) with the required evidence and an explicit NOT-sufficient column, because the common failures are near-misses like 'should work now' or 'it compiles', not outright lies.

nodes.label: Status tokens (DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / BLOCKED / NEEDS_CONTEXT)
nodes.rationale: Missing verification forces BLOCKED rather than DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, closing the escape hatch where an unproven result is downgraded instead of stopped; bad work is worse than no work.

nodes.label: Commit gate (a commit is a completion claim)
nodes.rationale: Treating `git commit` as a completion claim closes the loophole where work is committed without ever writing the word 'done', so the proving run has to happen before the commit, not after.

nodes.label: Debugging playbook (reproduce, two candidates, prove, falsify)
nodes.rationale: Requires two ranked candidate causes because the first idea is a candidate, not a diagnosis; reproduction comes first so nothing is fixed that was never seen failing.

nodes.label: Falsification step (revert the fix, the check must fail)
nodes.rationale: If the check still passes with the fix reverted, the check does not guard the behavior at all — the fix looked verified while the guard was vacuous, so the check itself is the defect to repair.

nodes.label: Three failed fix attempts -> stop, the frame is wrong
nodes.rationale: Repeated failure indicates a wrong framing of the problem rather than a wrong hypothesis inside a right frame, so more attempts inside the same frame cannot converge; escalate to the human instead.

nodes.label: Investigating playbook (enumerate, read, cite)
nodes.rationale: Enumerating candidates and stating the count before reading prevents stopping at the first plausible file; file:line citations make every claim checkable, and priors about how a framework 'usually' works are explicitly not evidence.

nodes.label: Unverified label (memory never speaks as fact)
nodes.rationale: Applies to casual conversation as well as work reports, because unmarked memory claims in chat are where fabricated specifics enter; for surfaces that cannot be observed from the session (another app's UI, a web dashboard) invention is banned outright since plausible is not real.

nodes.label: Implementing playbook (read region, small steps, tests, undo)
nodes.rationale: Reading the full touched region and running checks between behavior-preserving steps localizes any breakage to the last step, instead of leaving one large unverified diff at the end.

nodes.label: Assumptions ledger for vague requests
nodes.rationale: Writing 'Assuming: ...' and proceeding keeps work moving on ambiguity that does not change correctness, while only correctness-critical unknowns earn a question, grouped into one block to avoid drip-feed interrogation.

nodes.label: Declared adjacent edit
nodes.rationale: Adjacent edits are allowed but must be announced before they are made ('adjacent: <file> - <why>'), so scope creep is visible at the moment it happens rather than discovered in the diff.

nodes.label: Named undo before the first mutating edit
nodes.rationale: Naming the restore command before touching anything guarantees a rollback path exists while it is still cheap to establish; no named undo means no edit.

nodes.label: Cleanup sweep after delete / rename / move
nodes.rationale: A removal is only half done until the orphaned wiring is resolved — registrations (hooks, routes, DI, cron), caches and build outputs, DB queries and migrations, env vars and docs — so completion requires showing a zero-hit search count for the old name.

nodes.label: Scope restraint (a request is a contract)
nodes.rationale: A floor on invention, not on quality: handling for a case that cannot occur is dead code that reads as diligence, while error paths that can happen, edge cases and structured logs stay part of 'done'. A request that looks mistaken is flagged in one sentence and then done as asked, never quietly narrowed, widened or transformed.

nodes.label: Thinking out loud -> deliverable is the assessment
nodes.rationale: When the user is musing rather than requesting a change, the correct output is a report and a stop — acting on a thought that was not a request is itself a scope violation.

nodes.label: Long runs (autonomous, many steps without the user)
nodes.rationale: Remaining context is explicitly ruled out as a reason to stop or propose a fresh session, and a turn may never end on a plan or a promise, because both are the failure modes that make unattended work look finished when nothing ran.

nodes.label: Unattended pause rule (irreversible -> BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Splits the unattended decision by reversibility: an irreversible action stops the run with BLOCKED naming it, while a reversible and clearly implied one proceeds, so autonomy is bounded by consequence rather than by uncertainty.

nodes.label: Delegation criteria (independent AND sizeable)
nodes.rationale: A subtask finishable in a handful of steps costs a full context setup and buys nothing back; a verifier subagent is only useful for work the orchestrator did not watch, since re-checking self-proved work can only re-derive evidence already held.

nodes.label: Self-skepticism / inversion pass (PROVEN vs ASSUMED)
nodes.rationale: Every ASSUMED item is where a plausible claim usually breaks, so they are surfaced explicitly; verification must happen in a step separate from the one that wrote the code, because the writing step's own report is never evidence about itself.

nodes.label: Lessons ledger (~/.claude/conductor/lessons.md)
nodes.rationale: A falsified hypothesis or a confirmed real bug is appended as one `date | trigger | rule` line to a single machine-wide file, so every AI tool on the machine shares the same accumulated ledger instead of relearning per tool.

nodes.label: Choosing the approach (essence -> method)
nodes.rationale: Naming the dominant uncertainty first makes the method a consequence of the problem rather than of habit; when two essences compete the riskier one wins and must be named, and a method judged too heavy is shrunk in N or escalated to the user, never stripped of its spine (baseline, second candidate, separate critique).

nodes.label: Control group method for discipline artifacts
nodes.rationale: Rules, playbooks, injected prompts and lints are authored against failures measured WITHOUT them on 2-3 real tasks and then re-tested on the SAME tasks, because otherwise a rule is written against imagined failure modes; ordinary project docs are explicitly excluded from this heavier path.

nodes.label: Instrument first (reality disagrees with expectations)
nodes.rationale: Capture the real state before theorizing, then run one check chosen specifically to discriminate between the top hypotheses rather than a check that merely confirms the favorite.

nodes.label: Freshness ladder for possibly-stale knowledge
nodes.rationale: Ranks sources — artifacts and live payloads over official docs over blogs over memory — and rules memory out as evidence entirely, since model knowledge ages invisibly while the ranking stays stable.

nodes.label: Smallest reversible step for dangerous changes
nodes.rationale: Pairs a small step with a named undo and verification between steps, so the blast radius of any single mistake stays inside one reversible move.

nodes.label: Criteria first for creative or quality work
nodes.rationale: Writing down what 'good' means for this task before generating, and critiquing in a separate pass against those same criteria, stops the generator from grading its own output against criteria it invented after the fact.

nodes.label: Pin behavior first (refactor)
nodes.rationale: A refactor claims no behavior change, so current behavior is captured as tests or golden outputs first and re-run after each transformation step — the pin is what makes the claim checkable at all.

nodes.label: Reading and searching: rtk token economy
nodes.rationale: The rtk proxy compresses shell output before it reaches the model while built-in file tools bypass it, so reads and searches go through the shell; file EDITS are the standing exception and always use native edit tools, because edit precision beats token economy.

nodes.label: Language and reporting (plain Russian, no jargon)
nodes.rationale: Answers target a smart reader without a technical background; unavoidable technical terms keep their original names but get an immediate one-phrase explanation, and internal reasoning follows the reply language so the user can read it too.

nodes.label: Lead with the outcome
nodes.rationale: Brevity comes from selection (dropping what does not change the reader's next step), not from compressing prose into fragments, abbreviations or arrow chains; readability outranks brevity when the two conflict.

nodes.label: Re-ground the user after an unwatched stretch
nodes.rationale: The final message is the user's first look at everything, so the vocabulary built up during the work is treated as the agent's own and reintroduced; files, commits and flags each get a plain clause. An earlier statement is corrected only when the error would change the user's code, conclusions or decisions.

nodes.label: Under pressure (apply gates more strictly)
nodes.rationale: Time pressure, authority and sunk cost are the conditions under which gates are normally relaxed, so the rule inverts it: tighten instead, in one line. Disagreement and praise are not data — re-read the source, defend structurally correct work with facts, fix confirmed regressions immediately.

hyperedges.label: Evidence chain from claim to status
